title: Equip puts the ‘super’ into Supercars partnership
full_text:
Equip Super will become the official superannuation and retirement partner for Supercars across the remainder of the 2026 Championship, extending an arrangement that began earlier in the season.
The expanded partnership will give the fund a greater presence across race weekends, broadcasts and digital content, alongside fan experiences at the Bathurst 1000 and Gold Coast 500.
Supercars champion James Courtney will also join as a brand ambassador, with his involvement intended to make conversations about financial preparation and retirement planning more relatable to fans.
According to Equip Super, Courtney began thinking about his financial future early in his racing career and has remained closely engaged with his superannuation and longer-term plans. As he transitions from full-time racing into the next stage of his career, the fund said he brings first-hand experience of planning for retirement and life beyond full-time work.
Equip Super linked the partnership to its aim of helping members understand where their super is invested, check their progress and think ahead about the retirement they want.
The fund drew parallels between preparing for retirement and motorsport, pointing to the importance of preparation, adaptability, teamwork and decisions made over time.
Having joined Supercars during the opening rounds of the 2026 season, Equip Super said the extended arrangement would create a more consistent presence before, during and after race weekends.
Its involvement will continue through Pit Lane Preview presented by Equip Super, which examines key stories and strategies before racing, and Cool Down Lap presented by Equip Super, which provides post-race discussion and analysis.
The partnership will also include Super Movers, an evolution of the fund’s existing Biggest Mover integration that recognises drivers making progress through the field.
Equip Super’s announcement outlined plans for brand activations at the Repco Bathurst 1000, scheduled for 8–11 October, and the Gold Coast 500 on 23–25 October.
